label: History
value: Anne Shirley was mistakenly sent to Green Gables
unit: Anne Shirley was mistakenly sent to Green Gables to live with Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, who had requested a boy from the asylum. Upon arriving in Avonlea at eleven years old, she quickly formed a passionate friendship with Diana Barry and developed a fierce rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he called her 'Carrots' in class. Her dramatic antics led to various scrapes, including accidentally getting green hair from a peddler's dye and falling off a roof on a dare. Despite her impulsiveness, she saved Diana's sister Minnie May during a bout of croup, earning Mrs. Barry's complete forgiveness. Under the mentorship of Miss Stacy, she joined the Queen's class, tied with Gilbert for top entry marks, and ultimately won the prestigious Avery Scholarship at Queen's Academy. Following Matthew's sudden death and the threat of Marilla losing her eyesight, Anne chose to give up her college scholarship, stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla, and take up teaching at the local Avonlea school while finally reconciling her long-standing feud with Gilbert Blythe.

On his first afternoon back, he teases Anne Shirley by pulling her braid and calling her "Carrots," resulting in Anne smashing a slate over his head; despite taking the blame and apologizing, Anne refuses to speak to him. He engages in an academic rivalry with Anne, competing for the top of the class. Later, he rescues Anne from a bridge pile when her flat sinks during a game of Elaine, but she rejects his offer of friendship once again. At Queen's Academy, he studies for a First Class teacher's license, earning the prestigious Gold Medal upon graduation. Finding that his father cannot afford college, he plans to teach at Avonlea, but voluntarily gives up the position to Anne so she can stay at Green Gables with Marilla, taking a post at White Sands instead. Anne finally thanks him, and the two agree to become close friends.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet life.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet, introverted life at Green Gables alongside his sister Marilla. Due to advancing age and heart trouble, he and Marilla decided to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to assist with farm work. When Matthew drove to Bright River station, he discovered that a little girl named Anne Shirley had been sent by mistake instead. Reluctant to leave her at the station, he brought her home, falling under her charming personality along the drive and silently desiring to keep her. Matthew continually advocated for keeping Anne and indulged her far more than Marilla did, secretly buying her a puff-sleeved dress for Christmas with the assistance of Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Throughout her schooling, Matthew took immense pride in Anne's academic success and ambitions. Over time, his heart condition worsened while he continued to work hard on the farm. Upon reading a newspaper report announcing the sudden collapse of the Abbey Bank where all his savings were kept, Matthew suffered a fatal heart attack on the threshold of Green Gables and was buried in Avonlea.

When Matthew drove to Bright River station, he discovered that a little girl named Anne Shirley had been sent by mistake instead. Reluctant to leave her at the station, he brought her home, falling under her charming personality along the drive and silently desiring to keep her. Matthew continually advocated for keeping Anne and indulged her far more than Marilla did, secretly buying her a puff-sleeved dress for Christmas with the assistance of Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Throughout her schooling, Matthew took immense pride in Anne's academic success and ambitions. Over time, his heart condition worsened while he continued to work hard on the farm. Upon reading a newspaper report announcing the sudden collapse of the Abbey Bank where all his savings were kept, Matthew suffered a fatal heart attack on the threshold of Green Gables and was buried in Avonlea.

unit: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolmaster in Avonlea, where he spends much of his classroom time attending to sixteen-year-old Prissy Andrews under the guise of helping her with her lessons. When Anne Shirley attends school, he subjects her to public mortification by holding up her slate for poor spelling and forcing her to stand on the platform after she hits Gilbert Blythe for teasing her. The following day, he makes Anne sit with Gilbert as a scapegoat punishment for tardiness, prompting Anne to temporarily leave school. During his tenure, he whips Sam Boulter for talking back, leading to a confrontation with Sam's father. At an evening concert, he recites Mark Antony's oration over Cæsar's body while gazing at Prissy Andrews. On his final day of teaching at the end of June, he delivers a tearful farewell speech before leaving Avonlea school.

unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the main road of Avonlea, where she kept watch over all travelers entering or leaving town. Upon learning that Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert planned to adopt an orphan boy, she immediately visited Green Gables to investigate and express her disapproval of the risky venture. Two weeks after Anne Shirley's arrival, Mrs. Rachel visited Green Gables after recovering from a bout of grippe and insulted Anne's looks, prompting Anne to fly into an intense temper. The following evening, Anne made a dramatic apology to Mrs. Rachel, who readily accepted it and allowed Anne to gather lilies from her garden. Mrs. Rachel frequently gave Marilla advice on raising Anne and managing school issues, such as suggesting leniency during Anne's feud with Mr. Phillips. When Matthew sought help securing a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Anne for Christmas, Mrs. Rachel made it for him.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired by the Avonlea school trustees.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired by the Avonlea school trustees as the village's first female schoolteacher. She introduces dynamic teaching strategies, such as physical culture exercises, field days for nature study, student recitations, and composition exercises. In November, she organizes a Christmas concert with her pupils to raise money for a schoolhouse flag. She forms an advanced class after school to prepare interested students for the Queen's Academy entrance examination. Although offered a teaching position in her home district for the following year, she chooses to remain in Avonlea to see her students through their entrance exams. Under her guidance and strict preparation, all of her Queen's class candidates successfully pass their Entrance examinations.
